q: The ability of metals to be drawn into thin wires is known as: [JAC 2025]
e: Ductility is the ability of metals to be drawn into thin wires (gold is most ductile), while malleability is beating into thin sheets.

q: The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called:
e: Malleability allows metals like gold and silver to be hammered into very thin sheets.

q: Name a metal which exists in liquid state at room temperature: [JAC 2021]
e: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

q: Which non-metal exists in a liquid state at room temperature?
e: Bromine is the only non-metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature.

q: Which non-metal is a good conductor of electricity? [JAC 2021]
e: Graphite, an allotrope of carbon, conducts electricity well due to the presence of delocalised free electrons.

q: Which non-metal possesses natural lustre (shiny surface)?
e: Though non-metals are usually non-lustrous, iodine is an exception with a shiny metallic lustre.

q: Which metals are so soft that they can be cut easily with a knife?
e: Alkali metals like lithium, sodium, and potassium have low densities and are soft enough to cut with a knife.

q: Which is the hardest known naturally occurring substance?
e: Diamond, an allotrope of carbon, is the hardest natural substance and has an extremely high melting point.

q: Which metals are the best conductors of heat?
e: Silver and copper are the best conductors of heat, whereas lead and mercury are comparatively poor conductors.

q: Which pair of metals are poor conductors of heat?
e: Lead and mercury are poor conductors of heat despite being metals.

q: Why is sodium metal kept immersed in kerosene oil? [JAC 2021]
o: Because it is highly reactive and catches fire on exposure to air and moisture
e: Sodium reacts vigorously with oxygen and moisture at room temperature and catches fire, so kerosene prevents contact.

q: Which of the following is most reactive with water? [JAC 2026]
e: Sodium reacts violently even with cold water, producing heat enough to ignite the evolved hydrogen gas.

q: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide? [JAC 2024]
e: Amphoteric oxides (like Al2O3 and ZnO) react with both acids and bases to produce salts and water.

q: What is the name of the alloy formed by copper and zinc? [JAC 2020]
e: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc (Cu + Zn), whereas bronze is made of copper and tin (Cu + Sn).

q: Bronze is an alloy of:
e: Bronze consists of copper (Cu) and tin (Sn).

q: Solder, used for welding electrical wires together, is an alloy of:
e: Solder is an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point, making it ideal for joining electrical wires.

q: If one of the metals in an alloy is mercury, the alloy is known as:
e: Any alloy containing mercury as one of its constituents is called an amalgam.

q: The elements or compounds that occur naturally in the earth's crust are known as:
e: Naturally occurring elements or compounds in Earth's crust are minerals; those from which metals are profitably extracted are ores.

q: The unwanted earthly impurities like soil and sand present in mined ores are called:
e: Earthly impurities such as soil and sand contaminating mined ores are termed gangue.

q: Cinnabar (HgS) is an important ore of which metal?
e: Cinnabar (HgS) is the chief sulphide ore of mercury.

q: Heating sulphide ores strongly in the presence of excess air to convert them into oxides is called:
e: Roasting converts sulphide ores into oxides in excess air, whereas calcination heats carbonate ores in limited air.

q: The process of heating carbonate ores strongly in limited air to convert them into oxides is called:
e: Calcination decomposes carbonate ores like ZnCO3 into metal oxide and CO2 in limited air.

q: Pure gold is expressed as how many carats?
e: Pure gold is 24 carat; because it is very soft, 22 carat gold (alloyed with copper or silver) is used for jewellery.

q: Which metals are often found in the earth's crust in the free (native) state?
e: Least reactive metals at the bottom of the reactivity series like gold and platinum exist in the native state.

q: Which two metals have such low melting points that they melt if kept on the palm of your hand?
e: Gallium and caesium are metallic exceptions with very low melting points (~29–30°C), melting right on the palm.

q: Galvanisation is a method of protecting steel and iron from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of:
e: Coating iron or steel with a thin protective layer of zinc is called galvanisation.

q: Mixing iron with nickel and chromium produces which stainless alloy?
e: Iron alloyed with nickel and chromium forms stainless steel, which is hard and resistant to rust.

q: Which metal among the following is the MOST reactive?
e: Potassium sits at the very top of the standard metal reactivity series.

q: Which type of compound has high melting and boiling points and conducts electricity when molten or dissolved in water?
e: Ionic compounds have strong electrostatic attraction between ions (high m.p.) and free mobile ions in molten/aqueous states.

q: An element reacts with oxygen to give a compound with a high melting point that is also soluble in water. The element is likely to be: [JAC 2026 NCERT]
e: Calcium forms ionic CaO, which has a very high melting point and dissolves in water to form Ca(OH)2; CO2 is a gas and SiO2/iron oxide are water-insoluble.

q: Which of the following are NOT ionic compounds? (i) KCl, (ii) HCl, (iii) CCl4, (iv) NaCl [JAC 2025]
e: HCl and CCl4 are covalent molecules formed by electron sharing, whereas KCl and NaCl are ionic salts.

q: Why do solid ionic compounds NOT conduct electricity?
o: Ions are held firmly in a rigid structure and cannot move freely
e: In the solid state, electrostatic forces lock ions into fixed positions; mobility occurs only when melted or dissolved.

q: During the formation of magnesium chloride (MgCl2), how many electrons does one magnesium atom (Z=12) transfer?
o: 2 electrons (1 each to two Cl atoms)
e: Mg (2,8,2) donates its 2 valence electrons—one to each of two Cl atoms (2,8,7)—forming Mg²⁺ and two Cl⁻ ions.

q: Which metal does NOT react with cold water but reacts with hot water to form hydroxide and H2 gas (floating due to bubbles)?
e: Magnesium reacts with hot water (and steam), and hydrogen bubbles stick to its surface causing it to float.

q: Which set of metals reacts neither with cold nor hot water, reacting ONLY with steam?
e: Al, Fe, and Zn react only with steam to yield metal oxides and H2 gas; Pb, Cu, Ag, and Au do not react even with steam.

q: What is the balanced equation for the reaction of iron with steam?
e: Iron reacts with steam to form iron(II,III) oxide (Fe3O4) and hydrogen: 3Fe + 4H2O → Fe3O4 + 4H2.

q: Why does calcium start floating when dropped into water?
o: Bubbles of H2 gas formed stick to the surface of calcium metal
e: Hydrogen gas bubbles evolved stick to the surface of calcium, buoying it up to float.

q: What is the correct decreasing order of reactivity with dilute HCl for Mg, Al, Zn, and Fe?
e: Based on rate of H2 bubble evolution and heat rise, reactivity decreases as Mg > Al > Zn > Fe.

q: Why do most metals NOT evolve hydrogen gas when reacting with nitric acid (HNO3)?
o: HNO3 is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises produced H2 to water while reducing to nitrogen oxides
e: HNO3 is a powerful oxidising agent; it oxidises any H2 produced into H2O and reduces itself to N2O, NO, or NO2.

q: The process of forming a thick protective oxide layer on aluminium is known as:
e: In anodising, aluminium serves as the anode during electrolysis of dilute H2SO4, developing a thick corrosion-resistant Al2O3 layer.

q: Why can highly reactive metals like Na, Mg, and Al NOT be extracted by reducing their oxides with carbon?
o: These metals have greater affinity for oxygen than carbon does
e: Highly reactive metals hold onto oxygen more tightly than carbon can remove it, so they must be obtained by electrolytic reduction.

q: How is sodium metal extracted industrially?
o: Electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride (NaCl)
e: Molten NaCl undergoes electrolysis where sodium metal deposits at the cathode and Cl2 gas evolves at the anode.

q: In electrolytic refining of copper, what are taken as anode, cathode, and electrolyte respectively? [JAC 2020]
o: Pure Cu anode, impure Cu cathode, HCl
Impure Cu anode, thin strip of pure Cu cathode, acidified CuSO4 solution
Graphite anode, pure Cu cathode, NaCl
e: An impure copper block acts as anode, pure thin copper strip as cathode, and acidified aqueous copper sulphate as electrolyte.

q: During electrolytic refining of copper, the insoluble impurities settling beneath the anode are called:
e: Soluble impurities pass into solution whereas insoluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud.

q: After converting ZnS or ZnCO3 to zinc oxide (ZnO), which reducing agent is commonly heated with ZnO to obtain zinc?
e: Moderately reactive zinc is extracted by heating ZnO with carbon (coke): ZnO + C → Zn + CO.

q: How is copper obtained from its sulphide ore Cu2S?
o: Roasting in air to form Cu2O which then reacts with remaining Cu2S to give Cu
e: Cu2S is partially roasted to Cu2O, which then reacts with remaining Cu2S upon further heating: 2Cu2O + Cu2S → 6Cu + SO2.

q: In the thermit process used for welding broken railway tracks, aluminium powder reduces:
e: Aluminium reduces Fe2O3 exothermically to molten iron: Fe2O3 + 2Al → 2Fe(l) + Al2O3 + heat.

q: Why are platinum, gold, and silver chosen to make jewellery? [JAC 2026]
o: They are lustrous, malleable/ductile, and least reactive (resistant to corrosion)
e: They possess bright lustre, high malleability/ductility, and extreme resistance to tarnish or corrosion.

q: During extraction of mercury from cinnabar (HgS), roasting first produces which intermediate oxide?
e: Roasting HgS gives HgO, which further decomposes on heating to liquid mercury and oxygen.

q: Food cans are coated with tin and NOT with zinc because:
o: Zinc is more reactive than tin and may react with food acids
Zinc is less reactive than tin
e: Zinc is more reactive than tin and could react with organic acids present in food.

q: Why are ionic compounds soluble in water but generally insoluble in kerosene or petrol?
o: Water is a polar solvent that weakens inter-ionic attractions, whereas kerosene is non-polar
e: Polar water molecules stabilise separated ions, whereas non-polar organic solvents like kerosene cannot overcome strong ionic lattice forces.

q: Zinc oxide (ZnO) reacts with both HCl and NaOH. Identify the salts formed respectively:
e: ZnO forms ZnCl2 with HCl and sodium zincate (Na2ZnO2) with NaOH, demonstrating its amphoteric behaviour.

q: Why do noble gases like helium (2) and neon (2,8) stay chemically unreactive? [JAC 2024]
o: Their outermost electron shells are completely filled (duplet/octet complete)
e: Noble gases already possess stable filled outermost shells (2 for He, 8 for Ne/Ar) and have little tendency to react.

q: How do the electrical conductivity and melting point of an alloy generally compare with its pure constituent metals?
o: Electrical conductivity and melting point of an alloy are generally lower than pure metals
e: Alloying disrupts the regular metallic lattice, generally lowering electrical conductivity (e.g., brass/bronze vs copper) and melting point (e.g., solder).

q: Which metal can be extracted from its sulphide ore simply by heating in air without adding carbon?
e: Low-reactivity metals like mercury and copper are obtained from sulphide ores by roasting/heating in air alone.

q: When amphoteric aluminium oxide (Al2O3) reacts with NaOH, what salt is formed?
e: Al2O3 reacts with NaOH to produce sodium aluminate and water: Al2O3 + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO2 + H2O.

q: When metals produce a ringing sound upon being struck on a hard surface, this property is called:
e: Metals are sonorous—they ring when struck, which is why school bells are made of metal alloys.

q: Why are sulphide and carbonate ores first converted into metal oxides before reduction to the metal?
o: It is much easier to obtain a metal from its oxide than from its sulphide or carbonate
e: Reduction of metal oxides (by carbon or aluminium) is chemically much simpler and more efficient than direct reduction of sulphides or carbonates.

q: Why do tarnished copper vessels regain their shine when rubbed with lemon or tamarind?
o: Organic acids dissolve the basic copper carbonate green tarnish without harming pure copper
e: Citric/tartaric acid reacts with and dissolves the basic green copper carbonate patina, exposing the shiny copper surface underneath.

q: Identify the correct sequence of tarnish/corrosion colours on Iron, Copper, and Silver respectively:
e: Iron forms reddish-brown rust, copper forms green basic copper carbonate, and silver forms black silver sulphide.

q: An element X (atomic number 11) combines with element Y (atomic number 8). What is the formula and nature of the compound?
e: X (Na: 2,8,1) loses 1 electron to form X⁺, while Y (O: 2,6) gains 2 electrons to form Y²⁻; hence formula is X2Y (Na2O), ionic.

q: Metal A does not react with cold water, reacts with hot water, displaces Cu from CuSO4, and cannot displace Ca from CaCl2. Identify A:
e: Magnesium reacts with hot water (not cold), lies below calcium in reactivity, and above copper.

q: Iron nails are placed in tubes A (air + water), B (boiled water covered with oil), and C (dry air + anhydrous CaCl2). In which tube(s) will rusting occur?
e: Rusting requires both oxygen and moisture. Tube B lacks dissolved air and tube C lacks moisture, so rust forms only in A.

q: In the thermit reaction, how many moles of Al are required to completely reduce 1 mole of Fe2O3, and how many moles of Fe are formed?
e: From the balanced equation Fe2O3 + 2Al → 2Fe + Al2O3, 2 moles of Al react with 1 mole Fe2O3 to give 2 moles Fe.

q: Roasting a sulphide ore evolves a pungent gas X that is a major air pollutant causing acid rain. Identify gas X:
e: Roasting metal sulphides in air releases pungent sulphur dioxide (SO2) gas.

q: Metals P (extracted by electrolysis), Q (reduced by carbon), R (obtained by heating ore alone), and S (native state) have decreasing reactivity order:
e: Top-series metals require electrolysis (P), mid-series need carbon reduction (Q), low-series need only heating (R), and bottom metals are native (S).

q: What is the difference in chemical bonding between Cl2 gas and solid NaCl?
o: Cl2 has covalent bonding (electron sharing), while NaCl has ionic bonding (electron transfer)
e: Two Cl atoms share an electron pair in covalent Cl2, whereas complete electron transfer from Na to Cl creates ionic NaCl.

q: Which metal coating or alloy contains Zinc (Zn) without Copper (Cu) or where zinc acts as anode, vs brass/bronze/solder?
e: Galvanised iron consists of iron coated with zinc (no copper), whereas brass has Cu+Zn, bronze has Cu+Sn, and solder has Pb+Sn.

q: Pure iron is very soft and stretches easily when hot. Approximately 0.05% of which non-metal is mixed to make it hard and strong?
e: Adding about 0.05% carbon to pure iron makes it very hard and strong.

q: Even if the zinc coating on a galvanised iron pipe is scratched, why does the iron stay protected?
o: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so zinc corrodes preferentially instead of iron
e: Being more electropositive/reactive than iron, zinc undergoes sacrificial oxidation first, shielding exposed iron.

q: Name the non-metal used as electrodes in dry cells because of its high electrical conductivity:
e: Graphite conducts electricity via free electrons and has a high melting point, making it ideal for dry cell electrodes.

q: Element X has configuration 2,8,2 and Y has 2,8,7. Classify X, Y and the compound formed:
o: X non-metal, Y metal, covalent XY
X metal, Y non-metal, ionic compound XY2
e: X (2,8,2 = Mg) is a metal losing 2 electrons; Y (2,8,7 = Cl) is a non-metal gaining 1 electron, yielding ionic XY2.

q: Select the balanced equation for reducing MnO2 with aluminium powder:
e: Balanced equation: 3MnO2 + 4Al → 3Mn + 2Al2O3 + heat (3 Mn, 4 Al, 6 O on both sides).

q: Which of the following displacement reactions will NOT take place?
e: Copper lies below iron in the activity series and therefore cannot displace Fe from FeSO4.

q: To extract zinc from Calamine (ZnCO3) and Zinc blende (ZnS), what are their respective first thermal steps?
o: Calcination for ZnCO3 and Roasting for ZnS
Roasting for ZnCO3 and Calcination for ZnS
e: Carbonate ores undergo calcination in limited air while sulphide ores undergo roasting in excess air.

q: What is the nature of the aqueous solution of Na2O and its effect on red litmus?
o: Basic (forms NaOH), turns red litmus blue
e: Sodium oxide dissolves in water to form strong alkali NaOH, turning red litmus blue.

q: An element forms an ionic chloride XCl2 with a high melting point. X would most likely belong to the same group as:
e: Formula XCl2 indicates a divalent metal forming X²⁺ ions, matching Group 2 elements such as magnesium or calcium.

q: Gold does not dissolve in conc. HCl or conc. HNO3 alone, but dissolves in their 3:1 mixture called:
e: Freshly prepared 3:1 conc. HCl and conc. HNO3 is aqua regia, capable of dissolving gold and platinum.

q: Why do copper statues develop a greenish coating after years of open-air exposure?
o: Copper reacts with moist CO2 and O2 to form green basic copper carbonate
e: Exposure to moist atmospheric CO2 slowly corrodes copper into green basic copper carbonate.

q: Which of the following is NOT a method to prevent rusting of iron?
e: Immersing iron in salt water actually accelerates electrochemical rusting rather than preventing it.

q: Just as sodium is kept in kerosene, highly reactive white phosphorus (non-metal) is stored under:
o: Water, as it catches fire in air but does not react with water
e: Phosphorus reacts vigorously with atmospheric oxygen (catching fire) but not with water, so it is safely stored underwater.

q: Identify two gaseous non-metals at room temperature and one solid non-metal that has metallic lustre:
e: Hydrogen and nitrogen are gaseous non-metals at room temperature, while iodine (and graphite) are lustrous solids.

q: If molten NaCl is electrolysed instead of aqueous NaCl solution, what product forms at the cathode?
e: In molten NaCl there is no water to compete, so Na⁺ ions are directly reduced at the cathode to metallic sodium.

q: Both rusted iron oxide (Fe2O3) and basic copper carbonate (green patina) are basic in nature. What happens when treated with dilute acid?
o: Both react with dilute acid to form soluble salts and clean the surface
e: Both basic metal oxides/carbonates react with dilute acid to form soluble salts, cleaning off the surface layer.

q: The methods used to separate gangue from ore (enrichment of ores) are based on differences in:
o: Physical or chemical properties of the gangue and the ore
e: Concentration techniques rely on differences in physical (density, magnetism) or chemical properties between ore and gangue.

q: Which pair of metals reacts violently with cold water such that the evolved hydrogen immediately catches fire?
e: Potassium and sodium react violently and exothermically with cold water, instantly igniting the liberated hydrogen.

q: Moving down the metal reactivity series from K to Au, how does the chemical reactivity change?
o: Decreases steadily (tendency to lose electrons reduces)
e: Reactivity and tendency to lose electrons to form positive ions decrease down the activity series.

q: Why are solid ionic crystals typically brittle and shatter when hammered?
o: Applied force shifts crystal layers, bringing like-charged ions face to face causing repulsion and fracture
e: Pressure shifts ionic layers so like charges align and strongly repel each other, shattering the crystal.

q: 22 carat gold is harder than 24 carat gold because it consists of 22 parts pure gold alloyed with 2 parts of:
e: In India, 22 carat gold contains 22 parts gold alloyed with 2 parts copper or silver to give necessary hardness for jewellery.

q: For which set of metals is electrolytic reduction the ONLY practical method of extraction from ores?
e: Highly reactive metals at the top of the reactivity series (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) must be extracted by electrolysis.

q: Metal samples A, B, C, D are tested: A displaces Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag; B displaces Fe, Cu, Ag (not Zn); C displaces only Ag; D displaces none. Identify the LEAST and MOST reactive metals:
e: D displaces none (least reactive, like Ag/Au), whereas A displaces even Zn (most reactive).

q: Metal N catches fire in open air while metal P (phosphorus) is a non-metal catching fire in air. How are N and P stored respectively?
o: N (Sodium) under kerosene and P (Phosphorus) underwater
N in air, P in kerosene
e: Sodium reacts violently with water so it stays in kerosene; white phosphorus does not react with water so it is kept underwater.

q: To weld a cracked railway track, an engineer ignites a mixture of aluminium powder and a reddish-brown oxide. Which molten metal fills the crack?
e: Molten iron produced in the exothermic thermit reduction of Fe2O3 by Al fills and joins the cracked rail.

q: Why has the ancient Iron Pillar near Qutub Minar in Delhi resisted rusting for over 1600 years?
o: Ancient metallurgical technique and formation of a protective magnetic oxide surface film
e: As highlighted in NCERT, high-skill ancient iron processing created a protective surface oxide film preventing progressive rusting.

q: Select the correct three-step sequence to extract pure zinc from Zinc blende (ZnS):
o: Roasting → Reduction with carbon → Electrolytic refining
e: ZnS is roasted to ZnO, then reduced with carbon (coke) to zinc metal, followed by refining.

q: During the formation of MgO from Mg (Z=12) and O (Z=8), what ions are formed and which noble gas configuration do both achieve?
o: Mg²⁺ and O²⁻, both attain Neon (2,8) configuration
e: Mg loses 2 electrons and O gains 2 electrons, so both Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ attain the stable Neon (2,8) configuration.

q: Among Na2O, Al2O3, CO2, and SO2, which oxide forms salts with BOTH HCl and NaOH?
e: Al2O3 is amphoteric, forming AlCl3 with HCl and NaAlO2 with NaOH.

q: Magnesium (metal) and sulphur (non-metal) are burnt in air separately and their products are dissolved in water. Which solution turns red litmus blue?
e: Magnesium oxide forms basic Mg(OH)2 in water, turning red litmus blue; SO2 forms acidic sulphurous acid.

q: Which industrial surface treatment creates a durable, dyeable oxide layer on aluminium utensils and gadgets?
e: Anodising thickens the Al2O3 layer electrolytically, resisting corrosion and accepting decorative dyes.

q: Low-reactivity metal oxide decomposes on heating alone: 2HgO(s) → 2Hg(l) + O2(g). This thermal step represents:
e: Because mercury is unreactive, HgO is thermally unstable and decomposes directly into Hg and O2 on heating.

q: In a vessel made of which metal can aqueous copper sulphate (CuSO4) be safely stored without reacting?
e: Silver is less reactive than copper and will not displace copper or corrode the vessel; Fe, Zn, and Mg react and damage the container.

q: A student tests four metal-acid reactions and gets H2 gas in three of them. In which single case did H2 gas NOT evolve?
e: Copper is below hydrogen in reactivity and cannot displace H2 from dilute HCl, unlike Zn, Fe, and Mg.

q: Why are hardware components and musical/plumbing fittings often made of brass instead of pure copper?
o: Brass is harder, stronger, and more corrosion-resistant than soft pure copper
e: Alloying copper with zinc yields brass, which has greater hardness, tensile strength, and tarnish resistance.

q: In which metallurgical process are BOTH anode and cathode made of the same metal (one impure, one pure)?
o: Electrolytic refining of metals like Cu, Zn, Au
e: Electrolytic refining uses an impure block of the metal as anode and a pure thin strip of the same metal as cathode.

q: Does the mass of an iron rod change when it rusts in moist air?
o: Mass increases due to combination with oxygen and water molecules
e: Because oxygen and water chemically combine with iron to form hydrated ferric oxide, total mass increases upon rusting.

q: Among elements A(2,8,1), B(2,8,7), C(2,4), and D(2,8,8), which pair forms a covalent compound with a relatively LOW melting point?
o: C and B (forming CB4 like CCl4)
e: C (carbon) and B (chlorine) share electrons to form covalent CB4 (CCl4) with weak intermolecular forces and low m.p., whereas A+B form ionic AB.

q: Metal sulphide XS on heating in air produces an amphoteric oxide XO and gas SO2. Identify metal X and the heating process:
e: Roasting zinc sulphide (ZnS) yields amphoteric ZnO and SO2 gas.

q: XSO4 is pale green and YSO4 is blue. Metal X cannot displace Zn but displaces Y. What happens when metal Y reacts with concentrated HNO3?
o: Blue copper nitrate and brown NO2 fumes are produced
e: X is iron and Y is copper; copper reacts with concentrated HNO3 yielding Cu(NO3)2 and reddish-brown NO2.

q: In electrolytic refining of blister copper containing Zn, Fe, Ag, and Au impurities, where do these impurities end up?
o: More reactive Zn and Fe dissolve into electrolyte as ions, while less reactive Ag and Au settle as anode mud
e: More electropositive Zn/Fe oxidise into solution as ions without depositing at cathode, while noble Ag/Au fall unreacted as anode mud.

q: During electrolytic extraction of aluminium from molten alumina (Al2O3, m.p. >2000°C), what is added to lower its melting point and improve conductivity?
e: Adding cryolite lowers the melting point of alumina to ~950°C and enhances electrical conductivity.

q: On heating in air: metal P burns with dazzling white flame, Q forms a black coating without burning, and R shows no reaction even on strong heating. Reactivity order is:
e: P (e.g., Mg) is most reactive, Q (e.g., Cu) is less reactive, and R (e.g., Au/Ag) is least reactive: P > Q > R.

q: Equal strips of Fe, Cu, Al, and Zn are warmed in separate test tubes with concentrated NaOH solution. Which metals evolve H2 gas?
e: Only amphoteric metals like Al and Zn react with aqueous NaOH to produce sodium aluminate/zincate and H2 gas.

q: The black magnetic iron oxide Fe3O4 formed when iron reacts with steam is chemically a mixed oxide of:
e: Fe3O4 consists of one FeO (+2) and one Fe2O3 (+3) unit, hence called iron(II,III) oxide.

q: Both MgCl2 and CCl4 are chlorides, yet MgCl2 is a water-soluble high-melting solid while CCl4 is a volatile water-insoluble liquid. Why?
o: MgCl2 is ionic while CCl4 is covalent
e: MgCl2 is an ionic lattice (strong attraction, polar hydration) whereas CCl4 consists of non-polar covalent molecules.

q: If an ornament is hallmarked 18 carat gold, what percentage by mass of pure gold does it contain?
e: 18 out of 24 parts is (18/24) × 100 = 75% pure gold.

q: If a strip of magnesium (Mg) is dipped separately into aqueous Al2(SO4)3, ZnSO4, FeSO4, and CuSO4, in how many solutions will displacement occur?
o: All 4 solutions (since Mg is more reactive than Al, Zn, Fe, and Cu)
e: Magnesium stands above Al, Zn, Fe, and Cu in the reactivity series, so it displaces all four metals from their salt solutions.

q: Unlike covalent CH4 or HCl, what type of chemical bonding exists in sodium hydride (NaH)?
o: Ionic bond (Na⁺ cation and H⁻ hydride anion)
e: Electropositive sodium transfers an electron to hydrogen, creating Na⁺ and hydride H⁻ ions in an ionic lattice.

q: Why is roasting of a sulphide ore carried out below its melting point?
o: So air/oxygen has free access around solid particles without fusing into a molten lump
e: Keeping the ore solid below its melting point exposes maximum surface area to flowing air for complete oxidation.

q: Metal oxide M2O dissolves in water to form strong alkali MOH, and metal M is extracted only by electrolysing molten MCl. Identify M:
e: Formula M2O and MCl indicates a univalent alkali metal (M⁺) at the top of the reactivity series, such as Na or K.

q: What is the exact chemical formula of the green coating formed on copper after prolonged exposure to moist air?
e: Copper reacts with moisture, CO2, and O2 in air to form green basic copper carbonate: CuCO3·Cu(OH)2.

q: In anodising of aluminium to create a thicker oxide layer, which material acts as the ANODE and what is the electrolyte?
o: Aluminium article as anode and dilute sulphuric acid as electrolyte
e: Aluminium is made the anode in dilute H2SO4; oxygen evolved at the anode reacts with aluminium to build a thick Al2O3 coat.

q: Why do non-metals normally NOT displace hydrogen gas from dilute acids?
o: Non-metals are electron acceptors and cannot supply electrons to reduce H⁺ ions of acids into H2
e: Reducing H⁺ ions to H2 requires donating electrons; non-metals tend to gain rather than lose electrons.

q: Metal X reacts only with steam at high temperature, while metal Y does not react even with steam. Identify X and Y:
e: Iron reacts only with steam (forming Fe3O4 + H2), whereas copper, silver, and gold do not react even with steam.

q: Which atmospheric trace gas is primarily responsible for the black tarnish on silver articles?
e: Silver reacts with trace hydrogen sulphide (H2S) in the air to form a black coating of silver sulphide (Ag2S).

q: How many total cations and anions are present in one formula unit of Na2O?
e: Each formula unit of Na2O consists of two Na⁺ cations and one O²⁻ anion (total 3 ions).

q: Between the metal liquid at room temperature and the one melting on the palm, which one defines an "amalgam"?
e: An amalgam specifically refers to an alloy in which mercury (Hg) is one of the constituent metals.

q: During the electrolytic extraction of aluminium from molten Al2O3, at which electrode is pure molten aluminium collected?
e: Positively charged Al³⁺ ions migrate to the negatively charged cathode to gain electrons and form molten aluminium.

q: Why is freshly prepared Aqua Regia able to dissolve gold whereas neither conc. HCl nor conc. HNO3 can do it alone?
o: HNO3 oxidises gold while chloride ions from HCl form soluble [AuCl4]⁻ complex
e: Concentrated HNO3 acts as oxidiser while conc. HCl supplies Cl⁻ ions to stabilise gold as soluble [AuCl4]⁻ ions.

q: A student places Ag, Fe, Zn, and Pb rods into four beakers of blue CuSO4 solution. In which beaker does the solution turn completely COLOURLESS?
e: Iron forms pale green FeSO4 and Ag causes no change, whereas Zn forms completely colourless ZnSO4 solution.

q: Between roasting of sulphide ores and calcination of carbonate ores, which produces SO2 gas and which produces CO2 gas respectively?
o: Roasting gives SO2 and Calcination gives CO2
Roasting gives CO2 and Calcination gives SO2
e: Roasting sulphide ores releases SO2, whereas calcination of carbonate ores liberates CO2.

q: What distinguishes stainless steel from ordinary carbon steel in composition and property?
o: Stainless steel contains nickel and chromium with iron, making it rust-resistant
e: Adding nickel and chromium to iron yields stainless steel, which resists rusting unlike ordinary carbon steel.

q: An element Y (carbon) exists in two allotropes: one is the hardest natural substance and the other conducts electricity. Identify them: [JAC 2026]
e: Diamond (hardest natural substance) and graphite (good conductor) are crystalline allotropes of carbon.

q: During extraction of copper (2Cu2O + Cu2S → 6Cu + SO2), why does solidified copper have a blistered appearance ("blister copper")?
o: Escaping sulphur dioxide (SO2) gas bubbles during cooling
e: As molten copper cools and solidifies, trapped SO2 gas escapes, leaving blisters on the surface ("blister copper").

q: Among Li, Na, and K, which alkali metal reacts most vigorously with cold water?
o: Potassium (K), because its larger atomic size lets the valence electron be lost most easily
e: Down Group 1, increased atomic radius makes it easier to lose the outermost electron, so potassium reacts most violently.

q: Among Na, Mg, Fe, Cu, and Ag, which pair of metals will NEVER liberate H2 gas from dilute HCl?
e: Copper and silver sit below hydrogen in the activity series and therefore cannot displace H2 from dilute HCl.
